title: B2B Account Research Tools: Evidence and CRM Handoff
summary: Compare Salesmotion, Clay, Common Room and Demandbase on research evidence, CRM delivery, overwrite controls and the setup work behind each shortlist choice.
body_markdown:
A research tool can help a rep understand an account without supplying the fields your CRM workflows need. That distinction should shape both your shortlist and your implementation budget.


Salesmotion, Clay, Common Room and Demandbase approach account research from different starting points. The useful comparison is what a buyer can inspect, what an operator must configure, and what still needs a vendor answer before downstream teams depend on it.


Methodology: documentation-only comparison checked November 16, 2026, using eight original vendor sources, including partial technical extracts and a search excerpt where identified. No product trials or end-to-end CRM tests were performed; unknown means unresolved by these sources, not unavailable in the product.


## Match the shortlist to the work you need done


Tool


Shortlist when you need


Evidence behind that fit


Work to scope before purchase


Salesmotion


Account briefs and ongoing signal research for sellers


[Vendor assertion: cited briefs and original-source links for every insight](https://salesmotion.io/)


[Documented Salesforce setup](https://salesmotion.io/help/salesforce-integration-setup) : package, permissions, active mappings and selected accounts. Citation retention in mapped fields is unknown.


Clay


Research shaped around your own criteria and account context


[Vendor documentation: structured outputs, reasoning and distinct table/Account Agent workflows](https://www.clay.com/claygent)


[Documented setup](https://university.clay.com/docs/account-research-agents) : source, segment, instructions, output fields and approved external sync. Destination overwrite semantics remain unknown.


Common Room


Research using combined buyer and conversation context


[Vendor assertion: account/contact research, scoring and plays using unified context](https://www.commonroom.io/product/)


[Documented Salesforce setup](https://www.commonroom.io/docs/signals/business-integrations/salesforce-crm/) : integration user, mappings and update/create controls. Per-claim evidence payloads remain unknown.


Demandbase


Account intelligence for segmentation, prioritization and journey context


[Vendor assertion: first-party and third-party data, selectors, predictive models and journey stages](https://www.demandbase.com/products/account-intelligence/)


Outbound field mappings and delivery behavior need a separate implementation scope. The reviewed product page does not settle them.


Start with the output your existing stack lacks, then determine who will own its delivery and maintenance.


## Salesmotion: source-linked briefs, with separate delivery work


Salesmotion fits a seller-facing research brief requirement. Its[product page](https://salesmotion.io/) describes cited account summaries and explicitly promises that every insight links to its original source. That is a vendor assertion about inspectability, not a measured accuracy result.


An original-source link lets a rep check whether the underlying material supports an insight. It does not, by itself, explain why a qualification rule fired or establish that the URL reaches Salesforce with the summary. Citation retention in mapped CRM fields remains unknown.


The[Salesforce setup guide](https://salesmotion.io/help/salesforce-integration-setup) documents two distinct surfaces: a managed-package Lightning component and configured field synchronization. An operator installs the package, configures the trusted frame URL, grants access through a named integration user, chooses mapping directions, activates mapping rows and selects accounts.


The component can display research inside Salesforce. Persisted fields are the separate concern for reporting, routing and automation. Seeing intelligence on a record is therefore insufficient acceptance evidence for a workflow that reads ordinary Salesforce fields.


Timing also has two parts. Salesmotion[says it checks every account daily](https://salesmotion.io/) ; the[integration guide documents Salesmotion-to-Salesforce delivery every 12 hours, plus manual sync](https://salesmotion.io/help/salesforce-integration-setup) . Neither statement establishes the age of an underlying source fact or a maximum discovery-to-CRM delay.


Budget for a Salesforce administrator and a field owner, not just package installation. The guide says the package is included on Enterprise, with other plans requiring vendor enablement. Before committing, ask which brief fields and evidence URLs persist, who owns overwrites, and how failed writes appear. Those details remain unresolved here.


## Clay: configurable research, with reasoning and approval boundaries


Clay fits teams that want to define the research task and its output fields. Its[Claygent page](https://www.clay.com/claygent) distinguishes general-purpose agents in tables from Account Agents operating across account segments. Table research is described as stateless and on-demand or scheduled; Account Agents retain context and track changes.


Clay documents structured outputs and reasoning traces. The[Account Agent guide](https://university.clay.com/docs/account-research-agents) describes reasoning for agent-managed fields, including what the agent read and why a value changed. A reasoning trace helps an operator inspect a decision, but an original public URL attached to every extracted fact is unknown in these sources. Do not treat reasoning and citation coverage as interchangeable purchase criteria.


The documented setup starts with a connected source in Audiences, mapped fields and a segment. The operator then configures instructions, tools, context and output fields. Agent-managed values return to Audiences before human-approved CRM or warehouse synchronization. This gives RevOps meaningful control, while also putting research design and approval ownership into the implementation scope.


Plan entitlement needs its own check. The[pricing table](https://www.clay.com/pricing) lists CRM integrations on Growth and Enterprise, and warehouse connections on Enterprise.[Account Agent beta access includes Launch](https://www.clay.com/claygent) , but beta eligibility does not establish native CRM entitlement on that plan.


Clay's pricing table also separates source synchronization cadence by tier. That clock should not be read as a guarantee about agent completion or the freshness of every researched fact.


For budget planning,[Clay describes variable Data Credits plus one Action per account record processed by an Account Agent](https://www.clay.com/claygent) . Scope research depth, reruns and approval workload before estimating usage. Exact destination matching, overwrite behavior and retry semantics remain unknown in the reviewed extracts, so assign those questions to the integration owner before approving a rollout.


## Common Room: context-rich research and explicit field ownership choices


Common Room fits teams looking to research accounts and contacts using combined CRM, product, marketing, engagement and conversation context. Its[product page](https://www.commonroom.io/product/) asserts continuously updated buyer context and describes scoring models, plays and agent governance. These claims support evaluating contextual research; they do not establish an original URL or timestamp attached to every returned assertion.


Its[Salesforce documentation](https://www.commonroom.io/docs/signals/business-integrations/salesforce-crm/) provides a more specific setup boundary: inbound CRM context and outbound creation or updates for Leads, Contacts and Accounts. Salesforce Activities are documented as inbound-only. If your handoff depends on outbound Activity records, resolve that requirement separately rather than assuming all Salesforce objects behave alike.


Setup includes Salesforce API access, administrative access, integration-user permissions, field mappings and controls for enabling creation and updates. Those are operating decisions even when the connection itself is native.


The search-result excerpt for that[same Salesforce documentation URL](https://www.commonroom.io/docs/signals/business-integrations/salesforce-crm/) describes Allow Overwrite: enabled, it replaces the destination value on each sync; disabled, it fills only empty Salesforce fields.


The choice matters for ownership. Empty-field filling protects an existing value but can leave an old value untouched. Overwriting can replace a value another team maintains. Decide field by field whether Common Room or Salesforce is authoritative, and who can change that decision.


Budget for permission review and mapping decisions alongside the research configuration. The reviewed material leaves exact matching, delivery cadence, complete retry behavior and preservation of evidence URLs unknown. Ask for those specifics against your intended destination fields rather than treating a successful connection as implementation acceptance.


## Demandbase: account intelligence, with the delivery scope still to establish


Demandbase belongs on a shortlist when the missing layer is account intelligence for segmentation and prioritization. Its[Account Intelligence page](https://www.demandbase.com/products/account-intelligence/) describes firmographics, account hierarchies, intent, technographics and news or social triggers. It also claims to combine first-party CRM, marketing, email, calendar and website data with vendor data.


For implementation budgeting, separate data entering Demandbase from research leaving it. The reviewed page establishes the former at a product level; exact outbound objects, mappings, permissions, overwrite rules and delivery intervals remain unknown. Per-fact URLs and observation timestamps are also unresolved.


Keep Demandbase in scope when its intelligence model fits your requirement, and request a destination-specific implementation plan before comparing delivery effort with the other vendors.


## Turn the shortlist into an implementation budget


Budget by deliverable and owner before comparing subscription quotes. The sources support different levels of setup detail, so they do not justify a common implementation-hours estimate.


Budget item


Decision the estimate must include


Research design


Who defines the output, qualification rules, required evidence and rerun conditions? Clay explicitly puts agent instructions and fields in scope.


Destination access


Which plan, Salesforce permissions, integration user or vendor enablement is required? Confirm entitlement before configuration begins.


Data contract


Which objects and persisted fields receive research, reasons, URLs and timestamps? Separate display components from stored values.


Field ownership


Which values may be overwritten, which only filled when empty, and who resolves conflicts?


Ongoing operations


Who monitors failed writes, approves changes, reviews consumption and handles changed account status?


Research cadence and delivery cadence need separate acceptance criteria. A source publication date, the time a tool observed it, the last research run and the CRM write time answer different questions. Ask which timestamps are actually returned and stored before defining a freshness threshold.


Likewise, a score does not establish how the system handles insufficient evidence. If your team needs qualify, reject and unknown decisions, define them as your own requirements: enough evidence to satisfy a rule, affirmative disqualifying evidence, or insufficient/conflicting/stale evidence. Native support for that three-state model is unknown across this comparison.


## Resolve these questions before research drives outreach


Before budgeting the handoff, ask the relevant owners to resolve these questions and identify any configuration or implementation work:


-


Which account and destination record will receive the result, and how are subsidiaries and duplicates handled?


-


Can each required assertion retain its supporting URL, relevant dates and decision reason in the destination? Which parts remain in the vendor interface?


-


Where will qualification rules and an unknown state live, if the vendor does not supply the required model natively?


-


Which system prevents rejected or unresolved accounts from becoming outreach-eligible, and what happens when CRM status changes?


-


Where are customer, open-opportunity, do-not-contact, unsubscribe, duplicate and active-sequence exclusions enforced?


-


Who sees a failed write, retries it and verifies the final stored value?


Citation retention, cross-system suppression and automatic revocation of outreach eligibility remain unresolved in this review. Ask whether each control is already provided, needs configuration or requires implementation before adding it to the budget.


Choose the research output that fits your sellers, then approve the delivery scope separately. Ask the vendor to separate package installation or connector activation from mapping, field ownership and ongoing error handling in the implementation estimate.


## FAQs


### Which B2B account research tool should we shortlist for an existing stack?


Shortlist by the missing output: Salesmotion for cited briefs, Clay for configurable agent research, Common Room for unified buyer context, and Demandbase for account intelligence and segmentation. These fits follow the linked vendor material, not a comparative accuracy test. Confirm destination requirements before choosing.


### Is a reasoning trace the same as a source citation?


No. A reasoning trace describes how an agent reached or changed an answer; a source citation points to material supporting an assertion.[Clay documents reasoning](https://university.clay.com/docs/account-research-agents) , while[Salesmotion promises original-source links for every insight](https://salesmotion.io/) . Neither establishes that all evidence persists in your mapped CRM fields.


### Does research displayed in Salesforce become available to workflows?


Not necessarily.[Salesmotion documents both a Lightning component and field synchronization](https://salesmotion.io/help/salesforce-integration-setup) . Confirm which outputs are stored in normal fields, which remain in the component, and which your workflow can read.


### Can we protect existing Salesforce values during enrichment?


The search excerpt for[Common Room's Salesforce guide](https://www.commonroom.io/docs/signals/business-integrations/salesforce-crm/) describes disabling Allow Overwrite to fill only empty fields. This is excerpt-level documentation evidence, not tested behavior. Confirm the control for each mapping and establish which system owns corrections.


### Do these tools automatically keep unqualified accounts out of outreach?


That full cross-system behavior is unresolved here. Qualification or scoring claims do not establish how rejects, missing evidence or later CRM changes affect eligibility. Ask where exclusions are enforced, who owns the rule and how the destination records the result.
